newsitem.title: UK: EMAP succession seen settled in autumn.
newsitem.headline: EMAP succession seen settled in autumn.

text.p: Media company EMAP Plc is likely to announce the successor to chairman Sir John Hoskyns this autumn, analysts said on Monday.
Analysts said EMAP had spoken to them of an autumn announcement at a results briefing. Chairman Hoskyns has said he plans to retire after the company's annual meeting in July 1998.
Chief executive Robin Miller is seen as the most likely candidate to succeed Hoskyns, meaning his post will have to be filled.
Analysts said they were set to upgrade their forecasts for 1997/98 modestly, with a number nudging their pre-tax profit estimates above the 140 million stg level.

EMAP earlier announced a 40 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 121.1 million stg in the year to end-March. EMAP shares, which had gained 29p on Friday in anticipation of strong earnings, shed early gains to slip back 1p to 786.5p by 1200 GMT.
Nick Ward of Credit Lyonnais Laing said the issue of the succession was weighing on the share price.
"On the numbers alone they should command a higher rating," he said.

EMAP has been through a period of boardroom turbulence, the departure of managing director David Arculus to United News & Media in April following the ousting of two rebel non-executive directors last December.
Ward said he was likely to leave his current year profit forecast little changed at around 139 million and is looking for 156 million stg pre-tax in 1998/99.
"That is the crucial year when we see a possible turn in the UK advertising cycle and also see how the French economy is performing," he said.
Colin Tennant of UBS said he was likely to push his current year pre-tax forecast up from 138 million stg to a figure in excess of 140 million stg.
Robert Jolliffe of ABN Amro Hoare Govett also said a figure in the mid-140s stg was now possible.
